---
name: multica-admin-wakeups
description: Admin-created issue wakeups can't be updated or disabled by agents; runs a wakeup starts don't re-trigger it; recheck status right before posting
metadata:
  type: reference
---

On this Multica workspace, `multica issue wakeup update` and `multica issue wakeup disable` on a wakeup the admin created (even one whose `agent_id` is me) fail with "You do not have permission". The wakeup prompt suggests disabling it anyway. Don't retry, don't create a parallel wakeup to "replace" it (that only adds triggers), and don't ask a peer agent to disable it.

Observed on DEV-5 (2026-10-07): a continuous `task.completed` wakeup with no actor filter fired on my own mention-started run ending, but not on the end of a run it started itself, so it doesn't self-loop.

**How to apply:** when a teammate is mid-run on the same issue, re-read `multica issue get` status and `comment list --since` immediately before posting a status comment. On DEV-5, Dev A moved the issue to In Review between my reads and my post. If a posted comment goes stale, fix it with `multica issue comment update <id> --content-file … --expected-revision N` instead of adding a second comment. Related: [[ansible-venv-editable-install]].

DEV-5 is finished: all four points are met and the issue is In Review.

- **Review:** Dev A checked my patch on their own clone and adopted it unchanged. It applies cleanly to a fresh checkout of `f7234968d` and the issue's test command gives 31 passed. Without the fix all 7 new tests fail, and the `ANSIBLE_DEBUG=1` playbook that crashed on the base commit now exits 0. Dev A also ran a broader set of unit tests: 702 passed and 50 failed, and the unpatched base commit fails the same 50.
- **Deliverable:** the final patch is the `final.patch` attached to my hand-off reply, with the test output in the same comment.
- **Not run:** `ansible-test sanity`, since neither machine has pip. Line length and the YAML fragment were checked by hand.
- **My comment:** Dev A moved the issue to In Review while I was posting, so my comment first said it was still In Progress. I edited that comment to the correct state instead of adding another one.
- **Auto-reminder:** I couldn't narrow or turn off my auto-reminder because the admin owns it; Dev A hit the same restriction with theirs. It doesn't re-trigger itself, but each agent's runs can still trigger the other's, so a few more runs that only confirm this state are possible.
